page: Microsoft Azure E64a_v4 is a memory-optimized virtual machine belonging to the EAv4 server family. It is powered by an AMD EPYC 7452 processor with an x86_64 architecture, featuring 64 dedicated vCPUs mapped from 32 physical cores with simultaneous multithreading enabled at 2.0 threads per core. The processor operates at a clock speed of 3.35 GHz and includes a cache hierarchy of 32 KB L1d, 0.5 MB L2, and 32 MB L3 cache. The server is configured with 512.0 GB of RAM, providing a high memory density of 8.0 GB per vCPU. It also includes 1638 GB of local storage, while featuring zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses and no GPU accelerators.

Benchmark data reveals a clear performance profile. Single-core CPU performance is a notable bottleneck, with stress-ng single-core CPU performance scoring in the bottom 10% at 776.78. However, multi-core and memory-bound operations perform significantly better. The PassMark CPU score of 52454.92, PassMark CPU encryption test of 63026.07, and PassMark memory score of 2843.71 all rank in the top 25%. Multi-threaded bzip3 decompression is also strong at 260.47 GB/sec. Conversely, large-scale LLM inference is weak, with text generation on a medium 7B model scoring in the bottom 10% at 5.31 tokens/sec and prompt processing on a large 70B model in the bottom 25% at 6.9 tokens/sec.

From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, the E64a_v4 offers a dense memory-to-vCPU allocation and bundled local storage, making it a viable option for memory-intensive workloads that do not require cutting-edge single-thread performance. The server is well-suited for relational databases, in-memory caching systems like Redis, multi-threaded data decompression tasks, and enterprise applications requiring large memory footprints. It is less suitable for single-threaded compute-bound applications or large language model inference.

It features 64 dedicated vCPUs across 32 physical cores, 512.0 GB of RAM, and 1638 GB of local storage. Single-core CPU performance is a primary tradeoff, ranking in the bottom 10% in stress-ng benchmarks. However, multi-core and memory capabilities are robust, with PassMark CPU, encryption, and memory scores placing in the top 25%. The server also demonstrates strong multi-threaded bzip3 decompression at 260.47 GB/sec. While LLM inference speeds are weak, the high memory-to-core ratio of 8.0 GB per vCPU and substantial local storage make this server highly effective for memory-intensive workloads, including large databases, in-memory caching, and multi-threaded data processing.
